title: Chapter 10 — Eulipotyphla
description: Hedgehogs, shrews, and moles — small, largely insectivorous mammals that represent some of the most ancient placental lineages. Despite superficial similarities to rodents, eulipotyphlans are not closely related to them. Shrews have the highest metabolic rate of any mammal and must eat almost continuously to survive.

children.name: Erinaceus
children.description: True hedgehogs of Europe and Asia — iconic, spiny insectivores that have inhabited the Old World for around 15 million years. Their 5,000–7,000 hollow keratin spines are modified hairs, and when threatened a hedgehog can roll into a near-perfect ball by contracting the orbicularis muscle that runs around its back, protecting all exposed soft tissue. Hedgehogs are partial hibernators, entering torpor when temperatures drop and food becomes scarce. The Western European hedgehog has declined by roughly 50% in the UK since 2000, driven by agricultural intensification, habitat fragmentation, road mortality, and badger predation.

children.name: Erinaceus europaeus
children.description: The European hedgehog (Erinaceus europaeus), also known as the West European hedgehog or common hedgehog, is a hedgehog species native to Europe from Iberia and Italy northwards into Scandinavia and westwards into Ireland.

children.name: Erinaceus amurensis
children.description: The Amur hedgehog (Erinaceus amurensis), also called the Manchurian hedgehog, is a hedgehog similar to the European hedgehog in appearance and behaviour, although it is more lightly coloured.

children.name: Erinaceus roumanicus
children.description: The northern white-breasted hedgehog (Erinaceus roumanicus) is a species of hedgehog..

children.name: Erinaceus concolor
children.description: The southern white-breasted hedgehog (Erinaceus concolor), sometimes referred to as white-bellied hedgehog or white-chested hedgehog, is a hedgehog native to Eastern Europe and Southwestern Asia..

children.name: Atelerix
children.description: African hedgehogs — four-toed hedgehogs of sub-Saharan Africa and the Sahara. The African pygmy hedgehog (Atelerix albiventris) has become a popular pet worldwide, particularly in North America and Japan, though ownership is restricted in some US states. African hedgehogs tend to be smaller and more arid-adapted than their European relatives; some can aestivate during dry season in addition to hibernating in cold seasons. The four-toed hedgehog lacks the first toe on its hind feet, distinguishing it from European species.

children.name: Atelerix albiventris
children.description: The four-toed hedgehog (Atelerix albiventris), also known as the African pygmy hedgehog, is a species of hedgehog found throughout much of central and eastern Africa..

children.name: Atelerix frontalis
children.description: The Southern African hedgehog (Atelerix frontalis) is a species of mammal in the family Erinaceidae..

children.name: Atelerix sclateri
children.description: The Somali hedgehog (Atelerix sclateri) is a species of mammal in the family Erinaceidae.

children.name: Atelerix algirus
children.description: The North African hedgehog (Atelerix algirus) or Algerian hedgehog, is a mammal species in the family Erinaceidae native to Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya, Spain, Malta, and France..

children.name: Hemiechinus
children.description: Long-eared hedgehogs — a genus notable for their large, prominent ears that aid thermoregulation in hot desert environments. The ears radiate heat and provide acute hearing for detecting prey underground. These hedgehogs are faster runners than Erinaceus species and rely less on rolling into a ball, preferring to flee or jab at threats. They inhabit arid and semi-arid regions across Central Asia, South Asia, and North Africa.

children.name: Hemiechinus auritus
children.description: The long-eared hedgehog (Hemiechinus auritus) is a species of hedgehog native to Central Asian countries and some countries of the Middle East..

children.name: Hemiechinus collaris
children.description: The Indian long-eared hedgehog (Hemiechinus collaris) is a small species of mammal native to northern India and Pakistan..

children.name: Paraechinus
children.description: Desert hedgehogs — a genus adapted to some of the harshest arid environments on Earth, from the Sahara to the Thar Desert. Members have a characteristic dark mask or facial pattern and a bald patch on the crown of the head. They are highly insectivorous but also take scorpions and small reptiles. Their metabolic adaptations allow them to survive long periods without water, obtaining moisture from prey.

children.name: Paraechinus aethiopicus
children.description: The desert hedgehog (Paraechinus aethiopicus) is a species of mammal in the family Erinaceidae.

children.name: Paraechinus hypomelas
children.description: Brandt's hedgehog (Paraechinus hypomelas) is a species of desert hedgehog native to parts of the Middle East and Central Asia..

children.name: Paraechinus micropus
children.description: The Indian hedgehog (Paraechinus micropus) is a species of hedgehog native to India and Pakistan.

children.name: Mesechinus
children.description: Steppe hedgehogs — a small genus of hedgehogs native to East Asia, occupying the transition zone between temperate forest and the Mongolian steppe. They were formerly placed within Erinaceus but are now recognised as a distinct genus on genetic grounds. Distinguished by shorter ears and a more robust build compared to Hemiechinus, with which they share parts of their range.

children.name: Mesechinus dauuricus
children.description: The Daurian hedgehog (Mesechinus dauuricus) is a solitary small hedgehog.

children.name: Echinosorex
children.description: The greater moonrat — a single living species representing one of the most primitive members of the hedgehog family. Despite the common name, it is neither a rat nor a true mole but a large, naked-tailed insectivore with a distinct pungent ammonia-like odour used for communication and defence. Moonrats lack spines entirely, having instead coarse, bristly fur. They are the largest living erinaceids, reaching 1.4 kg.

children.name: Echinosorex gymnura
children.description: The moonrat (Echinosorex gymnura) is a southeast Asian species of mammal in the family Erinaceidae (the hedgehogs and gymnures)..

children.name: Podogymnura
children.description: Philippine gymnures — spiny-less erinaceids endemic to the Philippines. These small, shrew-like animals inhabit montane tropical forests. Like the greater moonrat, they lack spines and rely on scent glands for protection. The two known species are restricted to Mindanao and adjacent islands, representing a relict lineage that survived in isolated mountain refugia.

children.name: Podogymnura truei
children.description: Podogymnura truei, also known as the Mindanao gymnure, Mindanao moonrat, or Mindanao wood shrew, is a mammal of the family Erinaceidae.

children.name: Hylomys
children.description: Moonrats and gymnures — the most primitive members of the hedgehog family, lacking spines entirely. Moonrats superficially resemble large shrews or small opossums and represent the closest living relatives of true hedgehogs. The greater moonrat (Echinosorex gymnura) is the largest insectivore in Southeast Asia, reaching 40 cm in body length and smelling powerfully of ammonia. Gymnures are forest floor specialists of Southeast Asian rainforest; the lesser gymnure (Hylomys suillus) is one of the most abundant small mammals in the cloud forests of Borneo.

children.name: Hylomys suillus
children.description: The Javan short-tailed gymnure (Hylomys suillus) is a small mammal from the family of the Erinaceidae..

children.name: Hylomys dorsalis
children.description: The Bornean short-tailed gymnure (Hylomys dorsalis) is a gymnure..

children.name: Hemiechinus
children.description: Long-eared hedgehogs of Central and South Asia and the Middle East, distinguished by conspicuously large ears that aid heat dissipation in arid environments. They run faster than true hedgehogs and are less inclined to roll into a defensive ball, preferring to flee. Capable of short bursts of speed and are more agile climbers than European hedgehogs.

children.name: Hemiechinus auritus
children.description: The long-eared hedgehog (Hemiechinus auritus) is a species of hedgehog native to Central Asian countries and some countries of the Middle East..

children.name: Hemiechinus collaris
children.description: The Indian long-eared hedgehog (Hemiechinus collaris) is a small species of mammal native to northern India and Pakistan..

children.name: Mesechinus
children.description: Steppe and montane hedgehogs of Central and East Asia, sometimes called Daurian hedgehogs. Adapted to cold, open grassland and steppe habitats from Mongolia to northeastern China. Smaller than Erinaceus but with similar habits; hibernate deeply in winter in burrows dug into stiff soil.

children.name: Mesechinus dauuricus
children.description: The Daurian hedgehog (Mesechinus dauuricus) is a solitary small hedgehog.

children.name: Paraechinus
children.description: Desert hedgehogs of North Africa, Arabia, and South Asia — the most arid-adapted members of the family. Capable of surviving in true desert conditions by aestivating during extreme heat and drought. Their larger ears and paler colouration reflect their desert lifestyle. Often eat scorpions and other prey that other hedgehogs avoid.

children.name: Paraechinus aethiopicus
children.description: The desert hedgehog (Paraechinus aethiopicus) is a species of mammal in the family Erinaceidae.

children.name: Paraechinus micropus
children.description: The Indian hedgehog (Paraechinus micropus) is a species of hedgehog native to India and Pakistan.

children.name: Echinosorex
children.description: Monotypic genus containing the greater moonrat, the largest insectivore in Asia and one of the most distinctive members of the hedgehog family. Unlike its relatives it bears no spines, instead covered in coarse black and white fur. Produces an intensely musky odour resembling ammonia, used for territorial marking along watercourses.

children.name: Echinosorex gymnura
children.description: The moonrat (Echinosorex gymnura) is a southeast Asian species of mammal in the family Erinaceidae (the hedgehogs and gymnures)..

children.name: Neotetracus
children.description: Monotypic genus of primitive insectivores from southern China and adjacent Southeast Asia. The shrew gymnure superficially resembles a large shrew with its elongated snout and slender build, but belongs firmly within Erinaceidae. Represents one of the oldest lineages within the family.

children.name: Neotetracus sinensis
children.description: The shrew gymnure, or shrew hedgehog (Neotetracus sinensis), is a species of mammal in the family Erinaceidae and is the only extant species in the genus Neotetracus.

children.name: Talpa
children.description: True moles of Europe and Asia — subterranean insectivores with powerful, spade-like forelimbs for digging, a cylindrical, fur-covered body with no obvious neck, tiny vestigial eyes covered by skin or fused eyelids, and no external ear pinnae. The European mole can dig through 20 metres of soil per hour. Its fur lies in any direction, allowing the mole to reverse in its tunnel without resistance. Moles are solitary and aggressively territorial; males expand their tunnel systems dramatically in spring when searching for mates. The mole's blood contains a unique double-bonded haemoglobin that allows it to use CO₂-rich air in its burrow far more efficiently than surface mammals.

children.name: Talpa europaea
children.description: The European mole (Talpa europaea) is a mammal of the order Eulipotyphla.

children.name: Talpa caeca
children.description: The blind mole (Talpa caeca), also known as the Mediterranean mole, is a mole found in the Mediterranean region.

children.name: Talpa occidentalis
children.description: The Iberian mole (Talpa occidentalis) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae.

children.name: Talpa romana
children.description: The Roman mole (Talpa romana) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae.

children.name: Talpa stankovici
children.description: The Balkan mole (Talpa stankovici) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae.

children.name: Talpa levantis
children.description: The Levant mole (Talpa levantis) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae.

children.name: Talpa altaica
children.description: The Altai mole or Siberian mole (Talpa altaica) is a species of mole in the family Talpidae.

children.name: Talpa caucasica
children.description: The Caucasian mole (Talpa caucasica) is a mammal in the family Talpidae that is endemic to the Caucasus Mountains of Russia and Georgia.

children.name: Talpa davidiana
children.description: Père David's mole (Talpa davidiana) is a mole found in the Middle East, ranging from south-central Turkey east to Kurdistan Province, Iran, although it could also range south into Syria..

children.name: Talpa aquitania
children.description: The Aquitanian mole (Talpa aquitania) is a species of small burrowing mammal of the family Talpidae.

children.name: Talpa martinorum
children.description: Martino's mole (Talpa martinorum) is a species of small blind mole in the family Talpidae found in eastern Thrace along the western Black Sea coast in south-eastern Bulgaria and north-eastern Turkey, mainly in the Strandzha mountain range..

children.name: Talpa streeti
children.description: Père David's mole (Talpa davidiana) is a mole found in the Middle East, ranging from south-central Turkey east to Kurdistan Province, Iran, although it could also range south into Syria..

children.name: Condylura
children.description: The star-nosed mole — one of the most extraordinary mammals on Earth, found in wet, low-lying ground in eastern North America. Its nose bears 22 fleshy, pink tentacles arranged in a star pattern, containing over 25,000 minute sensory receptors (Eimer's organs) — the most sensitive touch organ of any mammal. The star-nosed mole is the world's fastest-eating mammal, able to identify and consume prey in as little as 120 milliseconds — faster than the human eye can follow. It is also semi-aquatic, swimming through streams and foraging under ice in winter using its extraordinary nasal sense.

children.name: Condylura cristata
children.description: The star-nosed mole (Condylura cristata) is a small semiaquatic mole found in moist, low elevation areas in the northeastern parts of North America..

children.name: Desmana
children.description: The Russian desman — an ancient, semi-aquatic insectivore related to moles but specialised for life in rivers and streams. With its long, flexible, trunk-like snout bearing Eimer's organs, webbed feet, and a flattened, scaly tail used as a rudder, the desman is one of the most bizarre mammals in Europe. It is now critically endangered — its range has contracted dramatically due to water pollution, river engineering, and mink predation. Fewer than 30,000 individuals may remain in the Don, Volga, and Ural river basins.

children.name: Desmana moschata
children.description: The Russian desman (Desmana moschata; vykhukhol ) is a small semiaquatic mammal that inhabits the Volga, Don and Ural River basins in Russia.

children.name: Galemys
children.description: The Pyrenean desman — a small, semi-aquatic insectivore endemic to the mountain streams of the Pyrenees and Cantabrian Mountains of Spain, Portugal, and southern France. Related to the Russian desman but only distantly, the two desman genera separated approximately 30 million years ago. The Pyrenean desman forages in fast-flowing, oxygen-rich mountain streams, using its long, flexible snout to probe among rocks for invertebrates. It is endangered due to water abstraction, pollution, and the introduction of American mink and signal crayfish.

children.name: Galemys pyrenaicus
children.description: The Pyrenean desman (Galemys pyrenaicus), also known as the Iberian desman or trumpet rat, is a species of small semiaquatic mammal in the family Talpidae.

children.name: Scalopus
children.description: The eastern mole genus of North America — robust, fully fossorial moles with broad, naked, paddle-shaped forefeet and a naked, short tail. The single living species is the most widespread mole in North America, found from the Great Plains to the Atlantic coast.

children.name: Scalopus aquaticus
children.description: The eastern mole or common mole (Scalopus aquaticus) is a medium-sized North American mole.

children.name: Scapanus
children.description: Western North American moles — larger and more powerfully built than eastern moles, occurring along the Pacific coast and Cascades. They inhabit moist soils and are significant ecosystem engineers in Pacific coastal forests and grasslands.

children.name: Scapanus townsendii
children.description: Townsend's mole (Scapanus townsendii) is a fossorial mammal in the family Talpidae, and is the largest North American mole..

children.name: Scapanus latimanus
children.description: The northern broad-footed mole (Scapanus latimanus) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Scapanus orarius
children.description: The coast mole or Pacific mole (Scapanus orarius) is a medium-sized North American mole found in forested and open areas with moist soils along the Pacific coast from southwestern British Columbia to northwestern California.

children.name: Parascalops
children.description: A monotypic genus containing only the hairy-tailed mole of northeastern North America. Distinguished by its distinctive, hairy tail — unlike the naked tail of most other North American moles.

children.name: Parascalops breweri
children.description: The hairy-tailed mole (Parascalops breweri), also known as Brewer's mole, is a medium-sized North American mole..

children.name: Mogera
children.description: Japanese and East Asian moles — a genus of medium-sized, fully fossorial moles found throughout Japan, Korea, China, and adjacent areas. Several species are island endemics with restricted ranges. They inhabit forested hills, agricultural land, and scrub.

children.name: Mogera wogura
children.description: The Japanese mole (Mogera wogura; 土竜 or コウベモグラ, lit.

children.name: Mogera imaizumii
children.description: The small Japanese mole, lesser Japanese mole or  Japanese Eastern Mole  (Mogera imaizumii) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Mogera robusta
children.description: The Ussuri mole It is found in China, North Korea, South Korea, and Russia and lives in a long burrow, seldom emerging on the surface of the ground during the day.

children.name: Mogera insularis
children.description: The insular mole (Mogera insularis) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae.

children.name: Mogera tokudae
children.description: The Sado mole or Tokuda's mole (Mogera tokudae) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae.

children.name: Mogera kobeae
children.description: The Japanese mole (Mogera wogura; 土竜 or コウベモグラ, lit.

children.name: Mogera minor
children.description: The small Japanese mole, lesser Japanese mole or  Japanese Eastern Mole  (Mogera imaizumii) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Mogera etigo
children.description: The Echigo mole (Mogera etigo) is an endangered species of mammal in the family Talpidae.

children.name: Euroscaptor
children.description: Asian moles distributed across South and East Asia, from the Himalayas through Southeast Asia to Japan. Distinguished from Talpa by various cranial and dental features; several species are montane specialists with restricted ranges.

children.name: Euroscaptor mizura
children.description: The Japanese mountain mole (Oreoscaptor mizura) is a species of Old World mole in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Euroscaptor klossi
children.description: Kloss's mole (Euroscaptor klossi) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Euroscaptor longirostris
children.description: The long-nosed mole (Euroscaptor longirostris) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Euroscaptor parvidens
children.description: The small-toothed mole (Euroscaptor parvidens) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Euroscaptor grandis
children.description: The greater Chinese mole (Euroscaptor grandis) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Euroscaptor malayana
children.description: Found in the highlands of Peninsular Malaysia, including Cameron Highlands and Genting Highlands. Restricted to montane forests above 1,000 m. One of the least-known mole species; IUCN Data Deficient.

children.name: Euroscaptor subanura
children.description: The Vietnamese mole (Euroscaptor subanura) is a species of talpine mole found in Vietnam.

children.name: Euroscaptor ngoclinhensis
children.description: The Ngoc Linh mole (Euroscaptor ngoclinhensis) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Urotrichus
children.description: Japanese shrew moles — small, surface-active moles of Japan that represent an intermediate between true moles and shrew moles. They forage both above and below ground and retain functional, though small, eyes.

children.name: Urotrichus talpoides
children.description: The Japanese shrew mole (Urotrichus talpoides) or himizu (ヒミズ) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Dymecodon
children.description: A monotypic shrew mole genus endemic to Japan, distinguished by its elongated tail relative to other Japanese moles. Represents one of the most ancient lineages within the family.

children.name: Dymecodon pilirostris
children.description: True's shrew mole (Dymecodon pilirostris) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Neurotrichus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the American shrew mole — the smallest talpid in North America and the sole member of its tribe Neurotrichini. It retains fully functional eyes and is highly surface-active compared to fossorial moles.

children.name: Neurotrichus gibbsii
children.description: The American shrew mole (Neurotrichus gibbsii) is the smallest species of mole.

children.name: Uropsilus
children.description: Chinese shrew moles — primitive, shrew-like talpids from montane forests of southwestern China and adjacent Myanmar. They retain long tails, small functional eyes, and are largely surface-active, representing an early branch of the talpid family tree.

children.name: Uropsilus soricipes
children.description: The Chinese shrew mole (Uropsilus soricipes) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Uropsilus gracilis
children.description: The gracile shrew mole (Uropsilus gracilis) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Uropsilus andersoni
children.description: The Anderson's shrew mole (Uropsilus andersoni) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Uropsilus investigator
children.description: The inquisitive shrew mole (Uropsilus investigator) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Uropsilus nivatus
children.description: The Snow Mountain shrew mole (Uropsilus nivatus) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Uropsilus aequodonenia
children.description: The equivalent-teeth shrew mole (Uropsilus aequodonenia) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Uropsilus atronates
children.description: The black-backed shrew mole (Uropsilus atronates) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Scaptonyx
children.description: A monotypic Asian genus containing the long-tailed mole — an intermediate form between shrew moles and true moles, with a longer tail than most fossorial talpids. Found in montane southwestern China and adjacent areas.

children.name: Scaptonyx fusicaudus
children.description: The long-tailed mole (Scaptonyx fusicauda) is a species of mole in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Scaptochirus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the short-faced mole of northern China — notable for its distinctively compressed, broad skull and very short rostrum compared to other talpids.

children.name: Scaptochirus moschatus
children.description: The short-faced mole (Scaptochirus moschatus) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Parascaptor
children.description: A monotypic genus from South and Southeast Asia containing the white-tailed mole — named for the pale tip of its tail. Formerly placed in Talpa or Mogera; now recognised as a distinct lineage.

children.name: Parascaptor leucura
children.description: The white-tailed mole (Parascaptor leucura) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae..

children.name: Scapanulus
children.description: A monotypic genus containing Owen's mole — found in the high mountains of central China. Scapanulus occupies an intermediate position in the talpid family tree, sharing features with both shrew moles and true moles; it has functional but reduced eyes and broader forelimbs than shrew moles, but is less completely fossorial than Talpa or Euroscaptor.

children.name: Scapanulus oweni
children.description: The Gansu mole (Scapanulus oweni) is a species of mammal in the family Talpidae endemic to central China, where it occurs in Shaanxi, Gansu, Sichuan, and Qinghai.
